Subject: Clarify billing for mixed short/long sessions

Hi team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looks great. Before we move our pilot to production we need one piece of clarity on billing: we send a mixture of very short single-turn assistant calls (100-200 tokens) and intermittent long consultation contexts (20k-40k) that re-use prefixes across calls. Our finance team is asking how Redwood accounts for this when minimums/flooring apply and how rounding is done across interleaved calls.

Concrete examples from our logs: 1) a burst of 250 one-off assistant calls over 30 minutes (each < 200 tokens) interleaved with 5 long retrieval-augmented sessions that maintain a 24k active context. 2) a long-running session that is periodically polled by nudge calls (1-3 calls per hour) — are those treated as the same context for min-flooring?

Can you:
- Confirm how minimums apply (per-request vs per-session) in hybrid usage patterns
- Show a short worked example / sample invoice line items for the two scenarios above
- Flag any rounding or carry-forward behavior that could materially affect our month-end charges

For reference I've attached a redacted sample invoice and usage extract.

Jared — thanks for the clear examples and the invoice.

Short answer: Redwood measures token consumption at the request boundary but groups tokens into billing "windows" when there is clear context reuse. For hybrid patterns we typically do the following (high level):

- Per-call tokenization: every API call is tokenized and counted at the time of the call.
- Active window grouping: if a call references an existing active conversation/context within a short time boundary (we call this the active window), tokens can be attributed to that context for amortized minimums.
- Minimums & rounding: minimums are applied at the billing object level (per-session bucket for active windows or per-request for isolated calls). Rounding is done on the aggregated token quantity per bucket; we do not round each request individually before aggregation.

To make this concrete we'll prepare a worked sample invoice mapping your logs to our billing objects. Quick clarifying Qs:
1) When you say "re-use prefixes" are these exact KV cache hits (exact token prefix reuse) or logical reuse where prompts are re-inserted? Exact reuse lets us apply stronger amortization.
2) For the long-running session with periodic nudges — what interval is "periodic"? If it is within our active window threshold (default 60 minutes for your account), nudges are part of the same billing window.

I'll loop Vanessa for the formal worked example and Camila for CS billing ops. If you'd like a provisional one-time credit for pilot noise while we validate the mapping, say the word and we can escalate.

—Rishi

> Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looks great.
>
> Concrete examples from our logs: 1) a burst of 250 one-off assistant calls over 30 minutes (each < 200 tokens) interleaved with 5 long retrieval-augmented sessions that maintain a 24k active context.

Thanks for the examples, Jared — I dug into this and prepared a compact worked example. I'm attaching a small spreadsheet (context-length-examples.xlsx) but the short math is below.

Assumptions (for example only):
- Active window threshold: 60 minutes
- Minimum billing quantum: 1,000 tokens per billing bucket
- Rounding: we aggregate tokens in a bucket and round up to the nearest quantum at invoice time

Scenario A — Burst + long contexts (simplified):
- 250 short calls x 150 tokens = 37,500 tokens total (isolated calls)
- 5 long sessions x 24,000 tokens = 120,000 tokens total (each is an active window)

Billing mapping options:
1) Conservative: treat short calls as individual billing buckets (no amortization) => short calls billed as ceil(150 / 1000) * 250 = 250 * 1,000 = 250,000 tokens billed (because each short call hits the 1,000 token minimum) + long sessions 5 * 24,000 = 120,000 => total billed tokens = 370,000
2) Amortized (preferred for reuse): group short calls into a single bucket if they share the same prefix/context within the active window. If grouped into 1 bucket: ceil(37,500 / 1,000) * 1,000 = 38,000 + long sessions 120,000 => total billed tokens = 158,000

Difference example: Conservative vs Amortized = 370k vs 158k billed tokens — large delta.

Scenario B — long-running session with nudges (polls):
- If nudges are within the 60-minute active window, they are credited to the session bucket and not billed as separate minimums. If nudges fall outside the threshold they create new buckets and could trigger new minimums.

Action items for us:
- Please confirm whether your short calls share exact prompt prefixes (helps with auto-grouping).
- If you approve, we'll run a redline mapping against your attached usage extract and produce a sample invoice with both conservative and amortized interpretations so your finance team can pick.

Attachment: context-length-examples.xlsx (XLSX)
